title: Create, Judge, Choose
tagline: This is your last KS3 year. You make real work, you learn to judge it, and you find out which kind of digital work suits you.

lessons.title: The Studio Opens
lessons.tagline: You see where this year leads, and you measure where you are starting from.
lessons.coverNote: This is the class's first-ever visit to the website, so the one-off Google permission screens land in this hour and they are far easier with the class's own teacher walking pupils through them. If cover cannot be avoided, printed credential slips (school office) should be to hand as a backup for pupils whose logins fail.

lessons.title: First Words in Python
lessons.tagline: Today you write your first computer code, in a language called Python, and make the computer print exactly the right words.

lessons.title: Playlist Engine
lessons.tagline: You hold a whole set of data in one place, using lists.

lessons.title: Function Factory
lessons.tagline: You package your code into functions you can use again and again.

lessons.title: Bug Bounty
lessons.tagline: You learn to find a fault in code, name it properly and fix it.

lessons.title: Data Newsroom
lessons.tagline: You question a set of data until it gives you a story worth telling.

lessons.title: Train Your Model
lessons.tagline: You find out how a machine learns a pattern from examples you give it.

lessons.title: The Intern
lessons.tagline: You use AI to help you write code, and learn where it cannot be trusted.

lessons.title: The Tribunal
lessons.tagline: You weigh up the real costs of AI and reach your own verdict on it.
lessons.coverNote: This hour is built around a whole-class debate, which is much harder to lead without knowing the class. The regular teacher is strongly preferred; if cover cannot be avoided, the on-screen work stands on its own.

lessons.title: Client Files
lessons.tagline: You turn what a real client asks for into user stories you can build from.

lessons.title: Prototype Sprint
lessons.tagline: You build a working prototype and test it against what the client actually asked for.

lessons.title: The Accessibility Audit
lessons.tagline: You test whether your work can be used by everybody, and fix what cannot.

lessons.title: Release Day
lessons.tagline: You plan the tests a real release needs, then write up how it went.

lessons.title: Studio Case: Multimedia
lessons.tagline: You try the Multimedia route for an hour and find out how it suits you.

lessons.title: Dev Case: Programming
lessons.tagline: You try the Programming route for an hour and find out how it suits you.

lessons.title: Both Routes, Side by Side
lessons.tagline: You put both GCSE routes side by side and see which one fits the work you like doing.

lessons.title: Graduation
lessons.tagline: You show how far you have come since your first hour in the Studio.
